name: apply 4 — application form: the applicant completes their OSE application

nodes.name: Form page 1
nodes.notes: Step 2 of applying to OSE. Page 1 asks only what the state lookup needs; everything structural was already validated by applying on Open Collective.

parameters.formDescription: The application form for fiscal hosting with Open Source Europe. It picks up from your application on Open Collective, so everything here is about the project itself.

values.fieldLabel: Contact email
Your collective's Open Collective URL
What are you applying as?

values.option: A group of projects, or an organisation behind several

parameters.completionTitle: That doesn't look like an Open Collective URL
parameters.completionMessage: We expected a link like https://opencollective.com/your-collective — the address of your collective's page on opencollective.com. Please open the form link again and paste that URL.

nodes.name: Application state
nodes.notes: The only page-1 checks the design needs: no row → apply on OC first; already submitted → first submission wins.

parameters.completionMessage: We could not find an application for that collective. Apply to Open Source Europe on Open Collective first: opencollective.com/europe/apply. Once you have, we will email you a link that brings you straight back here, so there is no need to return to this page on your own.

parameters.completionTitle: This application is already in progress
parameters.completionMessage: A form for this collective has already been submitted — the first submission wins, and a human will review it. If you think this is an error, reply to any email you received from us and a reviewer will sort it out.

values.fieldLabel: Repository URL
Project website (optional)
Licence
How does development happen in the open?
values.placeholder: Public issues and pull requests, roadmap, community calls, who maintains it…

options.formDescription: Where the code lives and how it is developed. This is what the human review reads first.

nodes.name: Persist page 2
nodes.notes: Answers are written after every page: an n8n multi-page form is one open execution, so a closed tab costs one page, not the whole application.

value.answers: ={{ JSON.stringify({ page: 2, submitted_at: $now.toISO(), responses: { applicant_type: $('Form page 1').item.json['What are you applying as?'] || '', repository_url: $json['Repository URL'] || '', project_website: $json['Project website (optional)'] || '', licence: $json['Licence'] || '', open_development: $json['How does development happen in the open?'] || '', community_home: $json["Where can we see the community's work?"] || '', community_open: $json['How is the community run in the open?'] || '' } }) }}

values.fieldLabel: Is the project already registered as a legal entity?
If yes, what kind and in which country?
values.placeholder: e.g. a German e.V., a Dutch stichting

values.fieldLabel: How long has the project been operating?
How much have you raised so far, if anything?
values.placeholder: Leave empty if you haven't started fundraising

values.fieldLabel: What is your target fundraising amount?
values.placeholder: A rough yearly figure is fine

values.fieldLabel: Who do you expect will fund the project?
values.placeholder: Companies using it, individual donors, grants…

values.fieldLabel: What do you expect to be your expenses?

values.html: It is important for us to know as it helps us understand the need of your collective.

values.fieldLabel: In which countries are most of the people who will be paid or reimbursed for expenses?

values.html: It is important for us to know as it can be harder to send money to some countries. If you don't know, just let us know where you and your team are located.

options.formDescription: Concise answers are fine — a sentence or two each.

value.answers: ={{ (() => { const page2 = JSON.parse($('Read the stored answers').item.json.answers || '{}').responses || {}; return JSON.stringify({ page: 3, submitted_at: $now.toISO(), responses: { applicant_type: page2.applicant_type || '', repository_url: page2.repository_url || '', project_website: page2.project_website || '', licence: page2.licence || '', open_development: page2.open_development || '', community_home: page2.community_home || '', community_open: page2.community_open || '', legal_entity: $json['Is the project already registered as a legal entity?'] || '', legal_entity_detail: $json['If yes, what kind and in which country?'] || '', operating_duration: $json['How long has the project been operating?'] || '', fundraising_to_date: $json['How much have you raised so far, if anything?'] || '', fundraising_goal: $json['What is your target fundraising amount?'] || '', funding_sources: $json['Who do you expect will fund the project?'] || '', expected_expenses: $json['What do you expect to be your expenses?'] || '', payee_countries: $json['In which countries are most of the people who will be paid or reimbursed for expenses?'] || '' } }); })() }}

values.fieldLabel: What does the project do?
values.placeholder: Briefly describe what the project and its community do

values.fieldLabel: How does the project further open source in Europe?
values.placeholder: Why Open Source Europe is the right home for it

values.fieldLabel: Anything else we should know?

nodes.name: Record submission
nodes.notes: The duplicate re-check happened on page 1; this write is what makes the next page-1 lookup say 'already in progress' — first submission wins.

value.answers: ={{ (() => { const page2 = JSON.parse($('Read the stored answers').item.json.answers || '{}').responses || {}; return JSON.stringify({ page: 4, submitted_at: $now.toISO(), responses: { applicant_type: page2.applicant_type || '', repository_url: page2.repository_url || '', project_website: page2.project_website || '', licence: page2.licence || '', open_development: page2.open_development || '', community_home: page2.community_home || '', community_open: page2.community_open || '', legal_entity: $('Form page 3').item.json['Is the project already registered as a legal entity?'] || '', legal_entity_detail: $('Form page 3').item.json['If yes, what kind and in which country?'] || '', operating_duration: $('Form page 3').item.json['How long has the project been operating?'] || '', fundraising_to_date: $('Form page 3').item.json['How much have you raised so far, if anything?'] || '', fundraising_goal: $('Form page 3').item.json['What is your target fundraising amount?'] || '', funding_sources: $('Form page 3').item.json['Who do you expect will fund the project?'] || '', expected_expenses: $('Form page 3').item.json['What do you expect to be your expenses?'] || '', payee_countries: $('Form page 3').item.json['In which countries are most of the people who will be paid or reimbursed for expenses?'] || '', activities: $json['What does the project do?'] || '', mission_fit: $json['How does the project further open source in Europe?'] || '', notes: $json['Anything else we should know?'] || '' } }); })() }}

parameters.completionMessage: Thanks — your answers are in and a confirmation email is on its way. A human will now review the application; that usually takes a few days, and you'll hear from us by email either way.

nodes.name: Render confirmation email
nodes.notes: DRY_RUN is checked here, at the send site. Template embedded verbatim from automation/emails/form-received.md.

nodes.name: Render submission thread reply
nodes.notes: Ready for evaluation. Slack always posts now, dry run included — the dry run protects applicant-facing email only.

nodes.name: Reply that the form was submitted
React with a clipboard on the parent
Ask apply 5 for a summary now

workflowId.cachedResultName: apply 5 — application summary: reads the project's README and summarises the form for reviewers

nodes.name: Which kind of applicant?
nodes.notes: Page 2 asks where the code lives, which a meetup has no answer to. The page 1 answer picks the page 2 the applicant sees. Only the community option leaves the original path, so an unexpected value still lands on the project page rather than being dropped.

nodes.name: Form page 2 for communities

values.fieldLabel: Where can we see the community's work?
values.placeholder: A website, past events, a repository of materials…

values.fieldLabel: How is the community run in the open?
values.placeholder: Open calls, public planning, who organises it, how people join…

values.fieldLabel: Project website (optional)

options.formDescription: Where the community's work is visible and how it is run.

nodes.notes: The community answer to the same question page 2 asks a project: where the work is visible, and how it is run in the open. It stores different keys from the project page, so apply 5 never treats a community website as a repository to fetch.

nodes.name: Read the stored answers
nodes.notes: Page 2 is now one of two nodes, so a later page cannot reach back to it by name: on the branch that did not run, the reference yields nothing and the answer disappears with no error. The row is what both branches wrote, so page 3 and the final write read page 2's answers from here.
